name: Soil pH
description: Logarithmic measure of hydrogen ion concentration in soil solution indicating acidity, neutrality, or alkalinity.

name: Soil Organic Carbon
description: Mass concentration of carbon stored in soil organic matter, key indicator of biological fertility, structure, and water retention.

name: Soil Moisture
description: Volumetric or qualitative water content held within the soil pore spaces available for microbial and plant root uptake.
directionality: higher_is_better (up to field capacity; waterlogging is detrimental)

name: Species Richness
description: The count or relative abundance of distinct flora, fauna, and soil macro/microbial taxa inhabiting the land parcel.

name: Habitat Diversity
description: Structural heterogeneity of the landscape, including vertical canopy tiers, field margins, ground litter, and ecological corridors.

name: Pollinator Abundance & Diversity
description: Presence, floral visitation rates, and nesting habitat availability for wild bees, butterflies, and other insect pollinators.

name: Water Availability & Precipitation
description: Effective precipitation regime, seasonal distribution, and drought recurrence governing soil moisture replenishment.
directionality: higher_is_better (balanced regime without extended arid droughts or prolonged ponding)

name: Temperature Regime & Thermal Stress
description: Thermal exposure, peak surface heat intensity, and evapotranspiration deficit affecting vegetative respiration and microbial survival.
unit: degrees Celsius or thermal stress class
directionality: lower_is_better (moderate temperatures without extreme heat spikes)

name: Chemical Pollution Pressure
description: Ecotoxicological load from synthetic pesticides, herbicides, and excess soluble synthetic nitrogen fertilizer application.

name: Deforestation & Clearing Pressure
description: Loss of woody vegetation cover, canopy removal, and clearing of native forest remnants fragmenting ecological corridors.

name: Agricultural Disturbance Pressure
description: Mechanical soil disruption, intensive inversion plowing, compaction from heavy implements, and lack of ground cover.
